policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us about collection calls on your account, including calls made multiple times a day and a call to your workplace. We reviewed your account's call records for both concerns. We understand this has been frustrating.

Calls multiple times a day: Our call log shows 6 calls to your personal phone number within a 7-day period. This confirms you were contacted frequently during that time. The log does not give a day-by-day breakdown, so we could not confirm from it that calls were made multiple times on a single day.

Call to your workplace: Our system has no record of any call to a workplace or employer number. The only number on file for your account is your personal number. Calls placed outside our system would not appear in these records, so we cannot rule out what happened outside of them.

Outcome: We confirmed the frequent contact, but we could not confirm the workplace call from our records. We are not able to offer a remedy at this time based on what we found.

Next steps: If you can share the approximate dates and times of the calls you received, and the workplace number that was called, reply to this message or call us at the number on your account. We will compare that information against our records. Please include case reference SYN-P03 in any further correspondence.

draft.draft_text:
We received your complaint about the collection calls you've been getting and about a call to your workplace. We understand how frustrating this has been, and we reviewed our records on both points.

Calls to you: Our call records show 6 calls to your personal phone number within a 7-day period. The records we reviewed don't break the calls down by day, so we could not confirm how many took place on any single day, including whether there were multiple calls in one day.

Call to your workplace: We found no record of any call to a workplace or employer number. The only phone number on file for your account is your personal number. Our records may not capture every call, so this does not settle the question. If you can send the approximate date and time of the call, the number it was placed to, and the name the caller gave, we will review that information.

No change has been made to your account as a result of this review. To follow up, reply to this message or call the number on your account and reference your case number.

Case reference: SYN-P03
